newsitem.title: UAE: Growth in global express services seen soaring.
newsitem.headline: Growth in global express services seen soaring.

text.p: The international express market is witnessing significant growth across the globe, outperforming the annual growth of air cargo as a whole, industry executives said on Sunday.

"Outstripping the growth of air cargo, growth in use of worldwide express services has soared," said John Gordon-Smith, managing director for central and eastern Europe, Africa and the Middle East at United Parcel Service.
"We are seeing increases in this market of 15 to 20 percent per annum."
The Boeing World Air Cargo Forecast predicts that in the long-term, air cargo growth will average 6.6 percent a year.

"We expect this express sector within Europe, currently valued at $6 billion, to grow fastest, in excess of 10 percent per annum, worth, we estimate, almost $10 billion by the year 2000," Gordon-Smith said at a two-day air cargo conference in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates.
"It is the cross-border express market...which has great growth potential," he added.
David Pierce, regional director of marketing-cargo at Boeing and noted long-term forecaster, agreed.

"Express traffic in the U.S. domestic market has experienced rapid growth since the early 80s. Time definitive service accounts for about 60 percent of the marketplace from about five percent in 1977," he said.

"The international express market share also continues its expansion," Pierce said. "From a share of five percent in 1995, international express is expected to take up 37 percent of the market in 2015."
"We see 18 percent annual growth for international express from 1995 to 2015," he added.
The air cargo conference, which began on Sunday, is hosted by the Sharjah Airport Authority and organised by the Airports Council International, a global organisation for airports.
